reason: This is the only offered action, and it should assemble the crane’s winding mechanism.
expectation: I expect a crank-driven drum with a ratchet wheel, though it may need a pawl before it can hold a load.

effect: The winch is assembled, and I understand how its crank winds the cord. It now needs mounting on the crane.
reaction: The trade-off between turning force and hand travel is a useful detail.
reason: Mounting the winch is the only offered combination and should bring the crane closer to lifting.
expectation: I expect the hand winch to attach to the crane frame, ready for the lifting cord.

effect: The winch is mounted on the crane, ready for the lifting cord.
reason: Adding the cord and hook is the only offered combination and should make lifting possible.
expectation: I expect the cord to connect the winch to the hook, probably passing over the boom pulley.

effect: The lifting line is fitted, so the crane is ready for a test load.
reaction: A straightforward step toward trying the mechanism.
reason: The test weight is the only offered combination and should show how the crane handles a load.
expectation: I expect the crane to lift the padded weight, though it may reveal a stability or holding problem.

effect: The frame is stiff, but the load makes the whole crane tip; it needs better balance before another lift.
reaction: The distinction between bending and tipping is a useful surprise.
reason: Rear ballast is the only offered combination and should counter the load's tipping effect.
expectation: I expect the ballast to weigh down the rear feet and make the crane more stable during a low test.

effect: The ballast keeps the feet on the bench during the low test, so the crane is stable enough to address holding the load.
reaction: The repeated test clearly shows what the ballast changed.
reason: The pawl and release lever are the only offered combination and should help the winch hold and lower a load.
expectation: I expect the pawl to engage the ratchet to prevent unwinding, with the lever allowing a controlled release.

effect: The pawl now holds the drum when winding stops; lowering requires holding the crank while easing the release lever.
reaction: The clicking pawl makes the holding mechanism easy to understand.
reason: The basket is the only offered combination and should test the crane on its intended load.
expectation: I expect to lift the basket, hold it with the pawl, and lower it carefully using the crank and release lever.

effect: The basket delivery demonstrated that the pawl holds the load and the crank and lever allow it to be lowered onto the stage.
reaction: Seeing the assembled mechanism complete the delivery is satisfying.
reason: The screwdriver is the only offered combination; it may release the crane from the bench clips.
expectation: I expect to undo the clips and free the finished crane, though I am not certain that will complete the goal.

effect: The crane is free of the bench and ready to move cargo at the stall; the lifting goal is complete.
reaction: Moving the finished crane to the fair is a fitting conclusion, though releasing the clips was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the load and adding ballast made the difference between a stiff frame and a stable crane clear; the repeated test showed the fix working.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the winch and adding the lifting line were straightforward assembly steps with little decision-making.

surprise.text: The frame stayed stiff while the whole crane tipped, making stability a separate problem from bending.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although every decision had only one offered combination, so I was following a prescribed sequence rather than choosing among mechanisms.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: the tipping test and pawl explanation made the mechanisms worth exploring, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
